title: figureforge recipe v1
description: The only thing a model may emit. A recipe names parts from a pinned kit and sets their parameters; it never contains code. Two kilobytes of JSON is the whole doll.

kit.description: exact catalog version. a recipe is invalid against any other kit, which is what makes an old doll reprint identically.

height_mm.description: printed height. the kit scales, the layer height does not.

rooms.description: one entry per room; a room is a category of part, not a screen.

^(hair|face|top|bottom|outerwear|shoes|h.description: an array because a slot can layer: a shirt under a jacket. ordering is layering order.

^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,23}$.description: one filament colour per slot. a part prints in exactly one colour.

palette.description: slot -> hex. the palette is data, so a recolour never invalidates geometry.

pose_mode.description: curated snaps to print-validated poses; free is preview and stl export only; articulated is a different kit, not a setting.

part.description: an id that must exist in the named room of the pinned kit. unknown ids are a vocabulary failure, not a fallback.

params.description: must satisfy the part's declared min/max/step, quantised to 0.01. the harness clamps nothing and guesses nothing: out of range is a failure.

colour.description: a palette slot name. a literal hex here is rejected so that recolouring stays a data change.

id.description: a curated pose id, or 'custom' when angles are supplied.

angles.description: joint limits live in the kit, not here. this schema only bounds what is physically expressible.
